description: Claim 1 is lab tests, and one of them charges the member 20% of its plan-approved amount. Note L1 on that line says laboratory services are covered in full under this plan. Claim 2, an office visit with lab tests, is correct. A careful reviewer should conclude, from the plan's own printed design, that the member owes $0 for that lab test.

sources.what: Under the rule that a plan must state its cost sharing, this plan charges $0 for covered lab tests, as Original Medicare usually does (note L1)
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(b)(2), Disclosure requirements (benefits and cost sharing), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111; Medicare.gov, Diagnostic laboratory tests, https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/diagnostic-laboratory-tests

sources.what: Medicare Advantage plans set their own cost sharing each year, and the evidence of coverage says what you pay
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Understanding Medicare Advantage Plans (CMS Product No. 12026), https://www.medicare.gov/publications/12026-understanding-medicare-advantage-plans.pdf

sources.what: For comparison, in Original Medicare you usually pay nothing for covered diagnostic lab tests
